title: OAuth revoke does not verify token ownership
description: api.rs:803-821. The POST /oauth/revoke endpoint accepts a token, hashes it, and revokes it without verifying that the revoking party owns the token. Per RFC 7009, the server SHOULD verify the client is authorized to revoke the token (Section 2.1). The endpoint also doesn't validate client_id/client_secret even though they're accepted in the request body (lines 798-800, marked dead_code). Any party who knows a token value can revoke it. In practice this is low risk because knowing the token already grants full access, but it deviates from the spec.
